title: Diabetes emergencies in the hospital: DKA, HHS and hypoglycemia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's diabetes (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)

Hospital Course:
Pt is a 75 y/o female with hx of type 2 diabetes. Presented to ED with altered mental status and fruity breath. Labs confirmed DKA. Pt was admitted to med-surg floor for stabilization. Managed with aggressive IV fluid resuscitation and continuous insulin drip. Blood glucose and electrolytes monitored Q1H. Pt showed prompt response to treatment; anion gap closed, and metabolic state stabilized. Pt tolerated diet and was able to ambulate. No acute distress noted prior to discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)
- Type 2 diabetes

Discharge Medications:
- Insulin glargine subcutaneous daily
- Metformin 500mg BID
- Oral fluids encouraged

Follow-up:
F/u with primary care in 1 week for lab work and DM management.

Electronically signed,
E. Castillo, MD
05/15/2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes with ketoacidosis without coma: E11.10 (HCC 36).

distractors.why: Ketoacidosis is a severe acute complication (HCC 36).
